plain: An attack that uses the model's internal weights and gradients, which is only possible when you have the model itself.
eli5: Picking a lock when you can see all the pieces inside it.
technical: An attack that requires access to model internals, such as gradient-based suffix search (GCG) or removing a refusal direction from the weights (Arditi et al. 2024), so it can run only on models whose weights the attacker holds; the opposite of a black-box (query-only) attack.
